chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Shurays al-Wābishī, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed jihad upon men and upon women. So the jihad of the man is that he gives his wealth and his blood until he is killed in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and the jihad of the woman is that she remains patient over what she sees of the harm of her husband and his jealousy.

key_terms.الرِّجَالِ: men; the male believers upon whom one form of jihad is ordained
key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women; the female believers who also have an ordained form of jihad
key_terms.الْجِهَادَ: jihad; prescribed struggle or striving in the path of Allah
key_terms.تَصْبِرَ: to be patient; to endure steadfastly
key_terms.دَمَهُ: his blood; his life given in sacrifice in the way of Allah
key_terms.غَيْرَتِهِ: his jealousy; the husband's possessive jealousy
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah; for Allah’s cause and path
key_terms.مَالَهُ: his wealth; material resources spent in the way of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the jihad of a woman according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that both men and women have a form of jihad ordained for them, though their expressions differ. For men, it is material and physical sacrifice in the way of Allah; for women, it is patient endurance within marital life, especially regarding harm and jealousy from the husband. The narration emphasizes duty, patience, and the different forms of struggle recognized in Islamic teaching.
